0067ca30.note: CDBCache lookup, 275 callers and the top of the seeds queue: given an id it returns the cached record when complete (flag at +0x220), otherwise allocates one and queues a server query, or appends the caller's callback to the pending list. Frozen's src/object/client/NameCache.cpp is a deliberate substitute for the name and creature caches, not a port of this: a name-by-object lookup with no callback list, no generic record store and no completion flag. Tagging it here would claim a contract Frozen does not implement. The item side hangs off the same machinery, which is why GetItemInfo, GetItemIcon, GetItemFamily, GetItemUniqueness and most of the 44 remaining CGTooltipScript stubs are all blocked on this one subsystem rather than on themselves. The chain for whoever builds it: SMSG_ITEM_QUERY_SINGLE_RESPONSE (0x58) is registered at 00635b40 to the handler 006354d0, which is a one-line forward into the generic cache parser FUN_0067cbd0(msg, cacheIndex). That parser reads a packed id, finds or allocates the record, and hands the payload to FUN_0098d910 -- the per-cache record reader, which is where the item wire format actually lives. Frozen can either port that machinery or write a bespoke item cache the way NameCache was done, but either way the field layout has to come out of FUN_0098d910.

00517020.note: Ported. Three calls the reference makes are deliberately absent, which is why the call-sequence score is low: the icon directory lookup (see 007e7cc0), the name-resolution cache FUN_0070a910, and the name-or-link resolver FUN_00709de0 that the string form of the argument needs. Two facts worth keeping: the argument is a DISPLAY id and not an item entry, since the lookup goes straight to ItemDisplayInfo rather than the item cache; and FUN_0070a910 is not a string transform but a cache keyed on the icon name that checks the file exists, so passing the name through unchanged gives the same answer whenever the file is present as named.

0061fec0.note: CGTooltip's shared add-a-line helper, taking left and right text together; 204 callers and the top of the world-spine queue after the big M2 and chat functions. It is the ON-DEMAND LINE CREATION frozen's CGTooltip.hpp already flags as missing: when the requested line is one past the current count it formats a region name with '%sTextLeft%d' from the tooltip's display name, creates a CSimpleFontString, and appends it, which is exactly how a tooltip grows past the eight lines GameTooltipTemplate.xml declares. Frozen splits the setting half across CGTooltip_AddLine, CGTooltip_AddDoubleLine and TooltipSetLine and does not create regions at all, so there is no single function to tag. Porting it is also the route to fixing the two-column overlap recorded at TooltipResizeToFit, since this is where the right-hand region is made and therefore where the reference must anchor it. ANCHORING, read out of it: the left region takes TOPLEFT to the previous line's BOTTOMLEFT at (0, -2), or to the tooltip for the first line; the right region takes RIGHT to the SAME line's left region at point LEFT with x=40. That is identical to what GameTooltipTemplate.xml declares, so the earlier claim that the reference re-anchors differently from the template was wrong and has been corrected at TooltipResizeToFit.

004a4350.note: Found by scanning .data for a pointer to the 'CopyFontObject' string and reading the function pointer beside it, because tools/recomp/data/ref-tables.jsonl does not contain this entry at all. The table it belongs to, 00ac1818..00ac1840, holds GetObjectType, IsObjectType, GetName, SetFontObject, GetFontObject and this one, and the export captured the first five but stopped before the last. Worth a look at the exporter: a truncated table is silent, and five of CSimpleFont's bindings looked unresolvable earlier in the session for the same reason.

00767460.note: Verified from GetCVarInfo (0050ff50), which calls it on the name argument and then tests the result's flags 0x40, 0x10 and 0x20 -- exactly what a registered-CVar lookup returns. Pinned because it came unlinked when the binding tables were widened: the extra table evidence reordered which rule claimed which Frozen name, and this one lost its automatic match.

00765880.note: 18 bytes, one callee (luaL_error) and the single string 'Access Denied' -- the shared refusal frozen registers for ReadFile, DeleteFile and their neighbours. Pinned because it came unlinked the moment a SECOND 'Access Denied' literal appeared in the port: GMRequestPlayerInfo raises the same text inline rather than calling this, which the reference also does, and the string rule cannot choose between two identical literals. The rule was right the first time; it just stopped being able to prove it.

00626240.note: Fills the spell body through TooltipSetSpellRec and stops. The reference fills these from FUN_00625f00, 814 bytes and 24 callees, which adds the remaining duration, the caster and a stack count on top of the spell text. Frozen has no tooltip line for any of those three, so the tooltip shows the spell but not how long is left on it -- a visible gap, recorded rather than papered over with an invented duration line.

00492e70.note: pinned: adding IsA call sites in the tooltip and scroll-frame bindings moved the automatic match to 0061ea00 (the tooltip module's own IsA) and took four neighbouring CSimpleFrame methods with it. The CSimpleFrame block is 00492c10-00492f10.

007dc010.note: structural only: the reference spells out thirty-one string comparisons in a row, this loops over the uniform Button4..Button31 tail. Same names, same flags. Low call-order fidelity is the metric seeing the loop, not missing behaviour.

005148b0.note: structural only: with no argument the reference asks after each of thirty-one buttons in turn; frozen keeps the same information as a bitmask in Input::s_buttonState, so that is one test. Same answers.

004d5550.note: the reference walks a registry of watchers, each holding its own copy of the bytes it watches; frozen has no registry yet and instead records which blocks actually changed as the first pass applies them, then signals the unit events the player and target frames need. Same effect for those fields, different mechanism, and narrower: only health, maxhealth, power, maxpower, level and faction, only for the player and target tokens. docs/ref/parity-mirror.md.

00815110.note: pinned 2026-09-19. It was linked by its two literals, HORIZONTAL and VERTICAL; moving them into a namespace-scope table shared with OrientationToString -- which is how the reference reads one table from both directions -- left the function itself mentioning neither, so the string matcher dropped it. The link is unchanged, the evidence for it moved.

005970f0.note: decompiled 2026-09-19: this is the character model's rotation setter -- it compares the new angle against the stored one, plays turn sequence 0xb or 0xc accordingly, raises a turning flag, stores the angle and records a now+100ms deadline. Frozen has no such method; Script_SetRotation writes CSimpleModel::m_facing directly. The callgraph matcher bound it to CGCharacterModelBase::GetObjectType, which it plainly is not.

00517890.note: the three validations are ported exactly; the measurement is not. The reference reads a per-frame script profiler through a virtual frozen has no counterpart for, so this answers zero time and zero calls -- nothing was measured, and FrameXML's profiling display divides by these, so nil would break it where zero reads as no cost.

0060c1f0.note: Pinned. Resolves a unit token to a guid then asks the object manager for it with TYPEMASK_UNIT (8), and its own assert string names ScriptEvents.cpp -- which is exactly what frozen Script_GetUnitFromName does. The callgraph matcher had put CGObject::GetGUID here, then swapped it to CGUnit::Unit when a binding edit changed a call sequence; both were wrong. CGUnit::Unit is a one-line accessor with no standalone address in the reference and is left unlinked rather than parked on 00513c30, which is a three-way roster lookup.

00610550.note: The swing time and both damage bounds are faithful. The three damage modifiers are read for school 0 where the reference derives the school from the equipped ranged weapon: it resolves the weapon's item id (FUN_006de330), looks the record up in the item cache (FUN_0067ca30), scans the damage entries at +0xc0 for the first with positive damage and takes its school from +0xd0. Frozen has neither the equipped-weapon lookup nor damage fields on ItemInfo. School 0 is correct for any physical ranged weapon and wrong for an elemental one.
